rituals.name: PURPOSE DAY OFF
rituals.goal: For one minute, your life is officially off duty from being profound.
rituals.mission: For one minute, your life is officially off duty from being profound.
rituals.rule: Guess what will go wrong if the next sixty seconds achieve absolutely nothing important.
rituals.one_rule: Guess what will go wrong if the next sixty seconds achieve absolutely nothing important.
rituals.play: Do one harmless purposeless thing: look at a spoon, straighten a cushion, stare out a window, doodle a shape. No lesson, no optimisation.
rituals.twist: Check whether meaninglessness for sixty seconds actually damaged anything.
rituals.mindBend: Your life can matter without every minute submitting a purpose statement.
rituals.mind_bend: Your life can matter without every minute submitting a purpose statement.
rituals.why: The pressure to make every moment matter can become heavier than the moment itself.
rituals.reveal: The pressure to make every moment matter can become heavier than the moment itself.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use this pass to loosen a rigid story about yourself, not to deny real needs, responsibilities, discrimination, abuse or other concrete circumstances. If the same pattern returns later, re-check the new context rather than copying today's answer.

rituals.name: THREE MEANINGS, SAME EVENT
rituals.goal: Same event. Three meanings. Let’s see which part is actually glued to reality.
rituals.mission: Same event. Three meanings. Let’s see which part is actually glued to reality.
rituals.rule: Guess whether you can make the event mean three different things without changing what happened.
rituals.one_rule: Guess whether you can make the event mean three different things without changing what happened.
rituals.play: Give the event three interpretations: one harsh, one boring, one unexpectedly generous. Don’t decide which is true yet.
rituals.twist: Notice that the facts stayed still while the emotional meaning moved.
rituals.mindBend: Events happen once. Meaning can be edited more than once.
rituals.mind_bend: Events happen once. Meaning can be edited more than once.
rituals.why: Meaning is often constructed after the event, not delivered inside it.
rituals.reveal: Meaning is often constructed after the event, not delivered inside it.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep this pass flexible rather than falsely positive. You do not need to replace one total identity verdict with another. Leave room for new evidence after the exercise instead of treating the result as final.

rituals.name: IDENTITY JACKET
rituals.goal: Take “I am” off for a second.
rituals.mission: Take “I am” off for a second.
rituals.rule: Guess which sentence feels heavier: “I am a failure” or “I’m noticing failure thoughts today.”
rituals.one_rule: Guess which sentence feels heavier: “I am a failure” or “I’m noticing failure thoughts today.”
rituals.play: Say the identity statement once. Replace “I am” with “I’m having the experience of…” or “today I’m noticing…”.
rituals.twist: Feel for any tiny change in permanence or tightness.
rituals.mindBend: A state can visit you without becoming your surname.
rituals.mind_bend: A state can visit you without becoming your surname.
rituals.why: Grammar can quietly turn a passing state into a definition of the whole person.
rituals.reveal: Grammar can quietly turn a passing state into a definition of the whole person.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use the sentence to make room around the story, not to force a preferred identity or minimise a real problem. A single pass can test the pattern; it does not need to settle it permanently.

rituals.name: FIVE-YEAR MUSEUM LABEL
rituals.goal: Imagine this problem behind glass five years from now.
rituals.mission: Imagine this problem behind glass five years from now.
rituals.rule: Guess what the museum label will mention—and what it will leave out.
rituals.one_rule: Guess what the museum label will mention—and what it will leave out.
rituals.play: Write a two-line label from five years ahead: “Object: the thing I was stressed about in 2026. What mattered later: ____.” Keep it factual, not inspirational.
rituals.twist: Notice what shrinks when the time horizon expands.
rituals.mindBend: Important now does not automatically mean important forever.
rituals.mind_bend: Important now does not automatically mean important forever.
rituals.why: Distance changes the size of details without claiming they are meaningless now.
rituals.reveal: Distance changes the size of details without claiming they are meaningless now.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use the written version as a test, not a verdict. Stop if you begin forcing the result or using it to ignore information that clearly needs action. Keep the result tied to this one example rather than generalising it to every situation.

rituals.recognition_cue: Current problem occupying the whole life story
rituals.theory_backbone: Temporal distancing; construal level theory; affective forecasting
rituals.mechanism_fingerprint: Recode a current stressor as a future museum artifact to induce temporal-construal shift.

rituals.name: TINY ENOUGH TO MATTER
rituals.goal: Pick something so small your ambition feels mildly insulted.
rituals.mission: Pick something so small your ambition feels mildly insulted.
rituals.rule: Guess whether a thirty-second action can still count as living a value.
rituals.one_rule: Guess whether a thirty-second action can still count as living a value.
rituals.play: Choose one value—care, courage, learning, honesty, health, creativity. Do the smallest visible action that matches it in under 30 sec.
rituals.twist: Check whether the action becomes meaningless merely because it was tiny.
rituals.mindBend: A compass still works when you only take one step.
rituals.mind_bend: A compass still works when you only take one step.
rituals.why: Values describe direction, not minimum order size.
rituals.reveal: Values describe direction, not minimum order size.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep the chosen example small, reversible and safe. Do not use momentum as a reason to ignore pain, exhaustion, major consequences or information that needs more thought. Stop at the planned endpoint rather than repeating the ritual until it feels completely convincing.

rituals.theory_backbone: ACT values; behavioural activation; goal scaling

rituals.name: FUNERAL FOR A RULE
rituals.goal: Some rules are alive only because nobody held the funeral.
rituals.mission: Some rules are alive only because nobody held the funeral.
rituals.rule: Guess where this rule came from before you decide whether it still belongs to you.
rituals.one_rule: Guess where this rule came from before you decide whether it still belongs to you.
rituals.play: Write the rule: “I must…” Under it, write the earliest place you remember learning it—family, school, or similar. Add: “Useful then because… Useful now because…”.
rituals.twist: Check if the rule still has a current job or only an old origin story.
rituals.mindBend: Old instructions can expire even when they were once useful.
rituals.mind_bend: Old instructions can expire even when they were once useful.
rituals.why: A rule can be inherited without being chosen.
rituals.reveal: A rule can be inherited without being chosen.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use the written version to reduce mind-reading, not to manufacture reassurance. Direct communication and boundaries carry more weight than guessed motives. If the same pattern returns later, re-check the new context rather than copying today's answer.

rituals.name: BORROWED GOAL DETECTOR
rituals.goal: Let’s check whether this goal is yours or merely renting space in your calendar.
rituals.mission: Let’s check whether this goal is yours or merely renting space in your calendar.
rituals.rule: Guess whose reaction matters most if you imagine quitting the goal tomorrow.
rituals.one_rule: Guess whose reaction matters most if you imagine quitting the goal tomorrow.
rituals.play: Imagine quietly stopping. Who appears first in your mind looking disappointed, impressed, confused or relieved? Name them. Ask what you would still want if nobody ever found out.
rituals.twist: Notice the gap between the audience goal and the private goal.
rituals.mindBend: If nobody could clap, what would still be worth doing?
rituals.mind_bend: If nobody could clap, what would still be worth doing?
rituals.why: Approval can power a goal without making the goal personally meaningful.
rituals.reveal: Approval can power a goal without making the goal personally meaningful.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Let the mental image create possibilities, not excuses. Keep direct words, consent, patterns of behaviour and your own boundaries in the picture. Keep the result tied to this one example rather than generalising it to every situation.

rituals.name: VALUE WITHOUT AUDIENCE
rituals.goal: Do one decent thing nobody can reward you for.
rituals.mission: Do one decent thing nobody can reward you for.
rituals.rule: Guess whether it will feel pointless if nobody sees it.
rituals.one_rule: Guess whether it will feel pointless if nobody sees it.
rituals.play: Choose a value and perform one invisible act: tidy something, send no photo, learn one paragraph, leave something kinder than you found it. Tell nobody for the next hour.
rituals.twist: Check if the action still feels aligned even without social proof.
rituals.mindBend: Some of the most honest choices are the ones that cannot earn applause.
rituals.mind_bend: Some of the most honest choices are the ones that cannot earn applause.
rituals.why: Visibility and value are different currencies.
rituals.reveal: Visibility and value are different currencies.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep the chosen example on the interpretation, not the other person's rights or limits. A kinder explanation does not cancel a clear no, repeated harm or needed distance. Keep the result tied to this one example rather than generalising it to every situation.

rituals.name: ROLE ON A COAT HANGER

rituals.mission: Take the role off for a minute.

GAME
IF NOBODY COULD FORCE YOU

GOAL
Take pressure out of the room for ten seconds.

ONE RULE

Imagine everyone affected would calmly accept either answer. Under that impossible freedom, what do you want?

Freedom is useful not because you always say no, but because it lets a real yes appear.

PAUSE

rituals.ritual_name: WHICH ONE MOVED: YOU OR THE STORY?
rituals.goal: Sometimes the choice happens first and the explanation gets hired afterward.
rituals.mission: Sometimes the choice happens first and the explanation gets hired afterward.
rituals.rule: Guess whether your opinion of a rejected option became harsher after you chose against it.
rituals.one_rule: Guess whether your opinion of a rejected option became harsher after you chose against it.
rituals.play: Take a past choice between two decent options. Recall what you liked about the rejected one before deciding, then what you said about it after.
rituals.twist: Check if the option changed—or your story about it did.
rituals.mindBend: A post-decision story can protect peace without being neutral history.
rituals.mind_bend: A post-decision story can protect peace without being neutral history.
rituals.why: We often reduce discomfort by upgrading our choice and downgrading what we left.
rituals.reveal: We often reduce discomfort by upgrading our choice and downgrading what we left.

rituals.move_on: ↻ WHICH ONE MOVED: YOU OR THE STORY?
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

rituals.name: WHEN AMAZING BECAME FURNITURE
rituals.goal: Something you once wanted badly may now be background décor.
rituals.mission: Something you once wanted badly may now be background décor.
rituals.rule: Guess one thing in your current life that past-you would have been thrilled to have.
rituals.one_rule: Guess one thing in your current life that past-you would have been thrilled to have.
rituals.play: Pick one ordinary possession, freedom, relationship, skill, routine or convenience. Imagine showing it to yourself five years ago.
rituals.twist: Notice the gap between present familiarity and past value.
rituals.mindBend: Boring can be what success feels like after your nervous system gets used to it.
rituals.mind_bend: Boring can be what success feels like after your nervous system gets used to it.
rituals.why: Repeated exposure reduces emotional intensity even when the underlying benefit remains.
rituals.reveal: Repeated exposure reduces emotional intensity even when the underlying benefit remains.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep the chosen example light and reversible. The exercise should widen perspective, not pressure you to deny facts or push through rising distress. Keep the result tied to this one example rather than generalising it to every situation.

rituals.name: HARD DOESN’T MEAN RIGHT
rituals.goal: The pain of getting here may be adding stars to the review.
rituals.mission: The pain of getting here may be adding stars to the review.
rituals.rule: Guess whether you would choose this path today if the effort already spent were erased.
rituals.one_rule: Guess whether you would choose this path today if the effort already spent were erased.
rituals.play: Imagine the same outcome arrived easily, with none of the sacrifice behind it. Do you still value the outcome itself as much?
rituals.twist: Check if effort and value are fused together.
rituals.mindBend: Something can be hard-earned and still not deserve more of your future.
rituals.mind_bend: Something can be hard-earned and still not deserve more of your future.
rituals.why: We often increase perceived value to make past effort feel worthwhile.
rituals.reveal: We often increase perceived value to make past effort feel worthwhile.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use the mental image as a test, not a verdict. Stop if you begin forcing the result or using it to ignore information that clearly needs action. The result is a working perspective, not proof that the opposite story is true.
rituals.precise_subpattern: Hard-won outcomes valued more because they were costly
rituals.preciseSubpattern: Hard-won outcomes valued more because they were costly
rituals.primary_trigger: Hard-won outcomes valued more because they were costly
rituals.challenge: Hard-won outcomes valued more because they were costly
rituals.recognition_cue: Hard-won outcomes valued more because they were costly
rituals.theory_backbone: Effort justification; cognitive dissonance; sunk cost
rituals.mechanism_fingerprint: Remove the history of effort from an achieved or pursued outcome and reassess the outcome's standalone value.

rituals.name: NEW DOESN’T MEAN FAKE
rituals.goal: A new behaviour can feel fake simply because your nervous system has no rehearsal history.
rituals.mission: A new behaviour can feel fake simply because your nervous system has no rehearsal history.
rituals.rule: Which feels more authentic: the old habit or the value you are only starting to practise?
rituals.one_rule: Which feels more authentic: the old habit or the value you are only starting to practise?
rituals.play: Name 1 behaviour that fits who you want to be but feels awkward: speaking up, resting, saying no, accepting praise, being warm. Imagine doing it ten times.
rituals.twist: Check if 'fake' starts to look like 'unfamiliar.'
rituals.mindBend: You can be sincere before a new behaviour feels natural.
rituals.mind_bend: You can be sincere before a new behaviour feels natural.
rituals.why: Familiarity contributes to the feeling of authenticity.
rituals.reveal: Familiarity contributes to the feeling of authenticity.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use the naming step to make room around the story, not to force a preferred identity or minimise a real problem. Stop at the planned endpoint rather than repeating the ritual until it feels completely convincing.

rituals.name: EVERY YES EATS SOMETHING
rituals.goal: That yes is not free.
rituals.mission: That yes is not free.
rituals.rule: Guess what this commitment displaces first.
rituals.one_rule: Guess what this commitment displaces first.
rituals.play: Take the yes you are considering. Complete: 'If I say yes, there will be less ___.' Name time, rest, money, attention, another project, family time, or recovery.
rituals.twist: Check if the decision changes when the invisible sacrifice becomes visible.
rituals.mindBend: A yes is also a no with better marketing.
rituals.mind_bend: A yes is also a no with better marketing.
rituals.why: Opportunity costs are easy to ignore because the rejected alternative is not physically present.
rituals.reveal: Opportunity costs are easy to ignore because the rejected alternative is not physically present.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use the example you picked for a low-stakes next step, not an irreversible decision. If the action has meaningful financial, medical, legal or safety consequences, slow down. Keep the result tied to this one example rather than generalising it to every situation.

rituals.name: WHAT MAKES YOUR WORLD BIGGER?
rituals.goal: Growth is not only climbing.
rituals.mission: Growth is not only climbing.
rituals.rule: Guess which experience would expand what you can do, notice, understand, or enjoy.
rituals.one_rule: Guess which experience would expand what you can do, notice, understand, or enjoy.
rituals.play: Choose one small expansion: talk to someone new, learn a tool, visit a place, try a cuisine, ask a question, make something badly.
rituals.twist: Notice how this differs from proving competence.
rituals.mindBend: A bigger life is not always a higher score.
rituals.mind_bend: A bigger life is not always a higher score.
rituals.why: Novel experiences can expand self-concept without needing status or mastery.
rituals.reveal: Novel experiences can expand self-concept without needing status or mastery.
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

rituals.ritualText:
PLAY TIME
75 sec

GAME
FORTIFY BEFORE FEEDBACK

GOAL
Feedback hits harder when one threatened area is pretending to be your whole identity.

ONE RULE
Guess whether the same criticism feels different after remembering a value you already live elsewhere.

PLAY
Before rereading one piece of ordinary critical feedback, name one unrelated value that matters to you and one recent action that expressed it. Reread the feedback.

TWIST
Check if the feedback becomes more specific and less identity-sized.

MIND BEND
You hear criticism differently when your whole worth is not standing trial.

SAFETY
PAUSE
Use this pass to test the added threat story, not to talk yourself out of a clear warning sign. Real hazards still get practical action. Leave room for new evidence after the exercise instead of treating the result as final.

rituals.recognition_cue: After choosing, the selected option becoming more attractive and the rejected option less attractive
rituals.unique_game_move: THE CHOICE STARTS EDITING THE OPTIONS
rituals.theory_backbone: Free-choice paradigm; cognitive dissonance; preference change
rituals.mechanism_fingerprint: Reconstruct pre-choice evaluations of chosen and rejected near-equal options and compare them with current post-choice ratings.
rituals.ritualText:
PLAY TIME
75 sec

GAME
THE CHOICE STARTS EDITING THE OPTIONS

GOAL
Once you choose, your brain may help you live with it by moving the ratings apart.

ONE RULE
Guess how you rated the winner and runner-up before the decision.

PLAY
For a recent close choice, reconstruct the pre-choice pros of the rejected option and cons of the chosen one before reading your current story.

TWIST
Check if the alternatives have drifted apart after commitment.

MIND BEND
A decision can change your preferences after it stops measuring them.

SAFETY
PAUSE
Keep this pass small, reversible and safe. Do not use momentum as a reason to ignore pain, exhaustion, major consequences or information that needs more thought. Leave room for new evidence after the exercise instead of treating the result as final.
